task: Query per-function type, ownership and effects of the functions of a package source file (churn pass of the B6 replay).
observation: `moss symbols|type|ownership|effects <target> --source <pkg>/src/<file>.moss --json` answers `MOSS_COMPILE_ERROR: interface for core is missing or stale; run `margo build`` even right after a successful `margo --check build` of that package, unless the caller sets MOSS_MODULE_PATH to the dependencies' build/check-debug directories the way margo does internally. Neither moss nor margo offers a package-aware query entry point, so the harness re-implemented the transitive path-dependency walk (churn.module_path_for). The error text points at `margo build`, which was already done.
impact: Every semantic query over package code needs a hand-built environment; an agent following the diagnostic would loop on margo build. Cost: one extra helper and a debugging detour.
evidence: moss inspect fn:starts_with --source sdk/text/src/text.moss --json without MOSS_MODULE_PATH

resolution.summary: Harness sets MOSS_MODULE_PATH like margo; a `margo query ...` passthrough or a message naming MOSS_MODULE_PATH would remove the detour.

task: Replay the last 50 SDK/packages commits against today's compiler with margo --check.
observation: Expected most historical trees to check; 39 of the 50 commits have at least one failing check today (92 of 149 checks fail), and 46 of those 92 are one diagnostic, TYPE_MISMATCH `push argument conflicts with the element type of 'parts'` in sdk/text and everything depending on it. The last four commits' post-edit checks all pass; the pattern is consistent with the Char/String SDK repair in commit dd45e307 but the cause was not diagnosed here.
impact: A history replay through today's compiler cannot be used as a clean latency or churn sample for most of the range; B6 records failures as frozen expectations and splits results by population, and only 14 of 50 commits are usable edits for the churn question.

resolution.summary: Old trees were written for an older compiler/SDK surface; this is a methodology limit, not a harness error.

task: Detect which function summaries an edit moves, including callers that were not edited.
observation: Durable entity ids (`entity-v1:function:...`) plus the three focused queries are enough to diff summaries across two trees without touching compiler internals: in a synthetic three-function file, a body change that makes `leaf` write its parameter changed leaf's access and effects and its caller `mid`'s access and effects (ripple), left an unrelated function unchanged, and a comment-only edit changed nothing. In the real replay, 4 of the 14 analysable edit commits moved summaries (ripple to callers of unedited functions in 2, both raises). Each query takes about 40 ms, so a 100-function package is a few seconds with parallel processes.
impact: Churn/ripple questions can be answered from the public query surface; a fact-store prototype can use the same fields as its invalidation oracle.

resolution.summary: Works as documented; the compared field set is listed in the README.

task: Observe type churn of unannotated (inferred-generic) functions.
observation: `moss type fn:leaf` of an unannotated generic function returns `_specialized_result:leaf` both before and after a body change that makes it return Float instead of Int (`return x + 1` -> `return x * 1.5`), so the `type` query does not expose the inferred result type of an open function; only annotated signatures and specialization records (via `inspect`) carry it. Not investigated further: whether `inspect`'s specialization records would show it in the packages replayed (almost all SDK functions are fully annotated).
impact: Type churn measured through `moss type` is a lower bound for unannotated functions; in the replayed SDK code this is probably negligible because functions are annotated, but that is not established.
evidence: moss inspect fn:leaf --source <file> --json on a three-function probe (leaf/mid/top)

resolution.summary: Left as a documented limit of the types category.
